Chapter Three: The Words Spoken from the Cross and Their Lasting Meaning.
The final hours of Jesus’ life are full of statements that, at first, might sound simple. But, if you really listen, each word from the cross carries a weight that stretches far beyond that moment. These words still offer comfort, challenge, and hope to anyone willing to hear them—even today.
Imagine this: in the middle of excruciating pain, Jesus’ first words are a prayer. Not for himself, but for the very people causing his suffering. Instead of anger, there’s a plea for forgiveness. That’s pretty remarkable, isn’t it? Most of us, when we’re hurt, want to hold on to resentment. But here, forgiveness is offered freely—before it’s even asked for.
It’s a powerful reminder: grace isn’t just for those who deserve it. It’s extended to everyone.
Then, there’s the conversation with a criminal hanging nearby. This man, with nothing left, simply asks to be remembered. And Jesus responds right away—no lecture, no requirements, just a promise of acceptance.
What does that say? Even in your darkest moments, hope is still possible. It’s never too late to turn toward grace.
In the midst of this suffering, Jesus looks down and sees his mother, standing with a friend. Even while pain wracks his body, his concern doesn’t fade. He makes sure the people he loves will be cared for. Isn’t that a beautiful detail? It shows us that real compassion doesn’t disappear when things get hard.
Love, true love, still sees and responds—even when it costs everything.
There’s also that heartbreaking cry of abandonment—a moment when Jesus feels the weight of separation from God. This wasn’t just about physical pain; it was the agony of feeling utterly alone. So many of us have had moments like this—when hope seems far away and God feels silent.
The cross doesn’t shy away from this reality. It gives voice to those deep fears and doubts. But, even in that darkness, the story isn’t over.
Then, there’s a simple phrase: “I am thirsty.” It’s such a human thing to say. The cross isn’t just about divine power—it’s about real suffering, real need.
If you’ve ever felt empty or longing, this moment connects with you. Admitting need isn’t weakness—it’s simply being human.
Finally, we come to the words, “It is finished.” These aren’t words of defeat—they’re words of victory. The mission is complete. The debt is paid.
For anyone who’s ever struggled with guilt, or felt like you have to keep earning your place, these words are freeing.
The cross declares that nothing more is needed. Grace is enough.
Every statement from the cross is like a window into the heart of God. They show us a love that forgives, a hope that endures, and a compassion that never fails.
If you’re willing to listen, these words just might change the way you see the world—and yourself.
